top_cited_works.title: Simultaneous sensing of temperature, CO, and CO2 in a scramjet combustor using quantum cascade laser absorption spectroscopy
MHz laser absorption spectroscopy via diplexed RF modulation for pressure, temperature, and species in rotating detonation rocket flows
Tomographic laser absorption imaging of combustion species and temperature in the mid-wave infrared
top_cited_works.abstract: In this work, laser absorption spectroscopy techniques are expanded in spatial resolution capability by utilizing a high-speed infrared camera to image flow fields backlit with tunable mid-wave infrared laser radiation. The laser absorption imaging (LAI) method yields spectrally-resolved and spatially-rich datasets from which quantitative species and temperature profiles can be generated using tomographic reconstruction. Access to the mid-wave infrared (3-5 µm) enables imaging of fuels, intermediates, and products of combustion in canonical small-diameter flames (< 1 cm). Example 1D measurements and 2D reconstructions of ethane (3.34 µm), carbon monoxide (4.97 µm), and carbon dioxide (4.19 µm) in an axisymmetric laminar flame are presented and discussed. LAI is shown to significantly enhance spatio-temporal data bandwidth (∼400 simultaneously sampled lines-of-sight) and resolution (∼50 µm) compared to other tomographic absorption spectroscopy techniques, and with a simplified optical arrangement.

recent_works.title: Benzene production from fires involving composite natural and synthetic fuel loads via laser spectroscopy
recent_works.abstract: Toxic emissions profiles from wildland–urban interface fires are changing with the adoption of synthetic construction materials that are making the fuel loads of such fires increasingly diverse. This paper presents a controlled atmosphere cone calorimeter experiment to quantify benzene production from composite fuel loads of common construction materials. Novel laser absorption spectroscopy methods are employed to measure benzene, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide with 1 Hz time resolution to track fire dynamics and evolution of speciation during fires with variable air vitiation. The measurement parameters are used to calculate a modified combustion efficiency and emission factors for benzene when paired with fuel mass loss measurement. The application of laser spectroscopy to these fire experiments represents an improvement over standard emissions measurement methods that lack time resolution, species specificity, and dynamic range to accurately quantify benzene production. Findings from this work aim to inform the creation of better models for WUI fire emissions and dynamics to better understand and mitigate the impacts of benzene production on first responders and affected...

recent_works.title: Hybrid THz-IR water and hydroxyl spectroscopy for sensitive thermometry and species detection
recent_works.abstract: A hybrid THz-IR, rotation-vibration laser absorption sensing method was developed for sensitive temperature, water and hydroxyl concentration measurements in combustion environments. A purely rotational H 2 O transition near 531 cm −1 (15.9 THz) and a transition in the R branch of the fundamental ν 3 vibrational band near 4030 cm −1 were chosen based on comparable absorption linestrength, spectral isolation, and a very large difference in lower quantum energy state ( Δ E ′ ′ = 4192 cm −1 ) for ratiometric thermometry. A neighboring rotational OH transition in the THz domain was selected for sensitive hydroxyl measurements with simultaneous water vapor sensing. Scanned-wavelength, spectrally-resolved laser absorption measurements at 25 kHz were achieved using a pulsed quantum-cascade laser (QCL) in the THz spectral domain multiplexed with a continuous-wave distributed feedback (DFB) diode laser in the IR. Thermometry performance was demonstrated in a shock tube for non-reactive argon-diluted water mixtures and reactive methane-oxygen mixtures from 1000 to 3800 K at pressures of 0.1 to 4 atm. Measured temperature accuracy was demonstrated to be better than 2% over the entire range...

recent_works.title: Toxicant production in under-ventilated compartment fires assessed by laser absorption spectroscopy
recent_works.abstract: The production of incomplete combustion products from the burning of wood, medium density fiberboard (MDF), and nylon in an under-ventilated compartment fire was investigated using a reduced-scale compartment. Species measurements of carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) were performed using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and methane (CH 4 ), hydrogen cyanide (HCN), benzene (C 6 H 6 ), ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) and acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) were measured with Laser Absorption Spectroscopy (LAS) with three different interband cascade lasers. The fuels were burned in three different crib configurations; only wood, only MDF, and a mixture of wood and nylon, to examine the production of different toxicants. During the experiments, measurements were collected of CO, CO 2 , CH 4 , HCN, C 2 H 2 , and C 6 H 6 species from the gas exiting the compartment, gas temperature from inside the compartment, and the flow into and out of the compartment. Consistent with under-ventilated combustion, the temperature inside the compartment typically exceeded 600 °C. recent_works.title: Minimizing Hydraulic Losses in Additively-Manufactured Impinging Liquid Rocket Injectors
recent_works.abstract: Hydraulic losses across a liquid rocket injector are undesirable, and are largely dependent on injector flowpath design. The expanded design freedom of additive manufacturing (AM) enables flowpath tapering which mitigates the inertial losses generally associated with sharp features within conventionally-manufactured injector geometries. However, the increased surface roughness inherent to AM parts can introduce additional frictional viscous losses, potentially offsetting the hydraulic benefits of the AM geometric optimization. Here, computational fluid dynamics simulations informed an iterative design to minimize hydraulic losses in a canonical conventionally-manufactured impinging rocket injector. Preliminary, smooth-wall steady CFD models exhibited how AM-enabled flowpath tapering, particularly applied to the orifice inlet, can improve injector discharge coefficient by significantly reducing inertial viscous losses, roughly +10% for the injectors modeled herein. Further computational analyses that account for surface roughness effects were performed to predict hydraulic performance, and a brief experimental validation effort was conducted. recent_works.title: Hydroxyl-Terminated Polybutadiene Reacting Boundary Layer Examined by Tomographic Laser Absorption Imaging
recent_works.abstract: Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) is a common fuel and binder for solid rocket propellants and hybrid combustion systems, yet predictive performance of these systems is challenging due to the complex multi-phase combustion phenomena. A lack of experimental data in the heterogeneous reaction zone near the burning surface of HTPB limits the ability to advance modeling efforts. This work uses laser absorption imaging (LAI) as a temporally- and spatially-resolved non-intrusive diagnostic method to examine the reacting boundary layer of HTPB. A tunable 4.98 μm continuous-wave quantum-cascade laser, targeting two carbon monoxide (CO) rovibrational transitions, is expanded into a 20 mm wide sheet that crosses the exit plane of cylindrical HTPB grains burning in an oxygen cross-flow. A mid-wave infrared camera recording at 73 kHz, with a window of 320×4 pixels, measures the light attenuation from molecular absorption inside the reaction zone, delivering simultaneous temperature and CO mole fraction data across 1280 lines-of-sight covering the entire axisymmetric flowfield.
